result:
All three operations are implemented correctly and the project builds cleanly with no warnings or errors.

The implementation adds three functions to `Spans.calr`, following the existing conventions (inline param form `([i32]:starts, ...)`, `§WH` loops with manual index, `§Q`/`§S` contracts, `§IDX`/`§LEN`):

- **`ContainsPoint`** — scans intervals, returns `true` on the first `starts[i] <= x < ends[i]` (half-open), else `false`.
- **`ClipCovered`** — clamps each interval to `[lo, hi)` (`a = max(starts[i], lo)`, `b = min(ends[i], hi)`) and sums `b - a` when positive; requires `lo <= hi`, ensures `result >= 0`.
- **`GapCount`** — counts consecutive pairs with `starts[i+1] - ends[i] > 0`; the `i < len - 1` bound naturally yields `0` for zero/one interval; ensures `result >= 0`.

`TotalCovered` is unchanged. The generated C# confirms correct half-open, clip-clamp, and gap semantics.
